job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his grandmother, Dadi, were walking through their village in Rajasthan when they saw a pile of trash near the pond. Rohan pointed at a discarded plastic bottle and asked if it would soon turn into soil like the fallen leaves nearby. Dadi shook her head, explaining that plastic is synthetic, made from petrochemicals, not natural sources like wood. She warned him that even when plastic breaks into tiny microplastics, it does not disappear or decompose; it simply becomes smaller, invisible pollutants that enter our food chain. Rohan noticed a cow chewing on a plastic bag and tried to shoo it away, knowing that land animals suffer just as much as sea creatures from eating these materials. Dadi then pointed to a neighbor burning a heap of plastic waste. She explained that this is dangerous because burning plastic releases toxic fumes into the air, which is far more harmful than burning organic wood. She emphasized that we must stop using single-use plastics, as they are designed for convenience but persist for centuries, and we cannot simply bury them or burn them to make them vanish. Recycling is helpful, but it is not a magic fix, as plastic quality degrades each time it is processed.

items.evidence: Dadi shook her head, explaining that plastic is synthetic, made from petrochemicals, not natural sources like wood.
items.q: Rohan thinks a plastic bottle will turn into soil like leaves. Why is he wrong?
options: It is man-made from chemicals, not nature
It is made from wood, so it rots slowly
It is one metal-like substance that never breaks
It is natural, but leaves rot faster
items.explain: Plastic is synthetic, made from petrochemicals, so it does not rot into soil like natural leaves.

wrong.why: thinks plastic comes from trees and plants
thinks plastic is a single substance like a metal
thinks plastic just disappears slower than leaves

items.evidence: She warned him that even when plastic breaks into tiny microplastics, it does not disappear or decompose; it simply becomes smaller, invisible pollutants that enter our food chain.
items.q: A plastic bag breaks into tiny pieces in a pond. What has happened to the plastic?
options: It is still there as smaller pollution
It has gone, since nothing can be seen
It has become tiny living things in water
It is harmless, as the pieces are too small
items.explain: Broken plastic does not disappear; it becomes smaller microplastics that stay in nature and enter the food chain.

wrong.why: thinks tiny pieces mean plastic has vanished
thinks microplastics are too small to harm

items.evidence: Rohan noticed a cow chewing on a plastic bag and tried to shoo it away, knowing that land animals suffer just as much as sea creatures from eating these materials.
items.q: Why did Rohan try to shoo the cow away from the plastic bag?
options: Eating plastic harms land animals too
Only sea animals get hurt by plastic
Cows cannot digest plastic that is dirty
The bag could pollute the pond water
items.explain: Land animals suffer just as much as sea creatures from eating plastic, so the cow was in danger.

wrong.why: thinks only sea animals are harmed
picks a made-up reason that sounds plausible
picks a nearby detail, the pond, as the reason

items.evidence: She explained that this is dangerous because burning plastic releases toxic fumes into the air, which is far more harmful than burning organic wood.
items.q: Why is burning a heap of plastic worse than burning wood?
options: It gives off toxic fumes into the air
It makes the plastic vanish too slowly
It burns the plastic into bigger pieces
It leaves ash that harms the soil
items.explain: Burning plastic releases toxic fumes into the air, which is far more harmful than burning organic wood.

wrong.why: assumes burning is slow, but the passage says it is toxic
thinks burning makes plastic only change size
picks an unstated side effect such as ash

items.evidence: Recycling is helpful, but it is not a magic fix, as plastic quality degrades each time it is processed.
items.q: Why is recycling plastic not a perfect fix for plastic waste?
options: Its quality drops each time it is recycled
It can be recycled again and again freely
Dirty mixed plastic is recycled just as well
The recycling symbol means it is recycled everywhere
items.explain: Plastic quality degrades each time it is processed, so recycling cannot solve the problem alone.

wrong.why: thinks plastic recycles forever without loss
thinks dirty mixed plastic can be recycled
thinks the triangle symbol means recyclable everywhere
